quests.question: My aunt is bringing ___ umbrella today because it might rain.
quests.sentence: My aunt is bringing ___ umbrella today because it might rain.
quests.hint: Say the word right after the gap out loud.
quests.explanation: 'Umbrella' starts with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'. We say 'an umbrella', not 'a umbrella'.

quests.question: I have a dog and a cat. ___ dog always sleeps on my bed.
quests.sentence: I have a dog and a cat. ___ dog always sleeps on my bed.
quests.hint: This dog was already mentioned once - point back to that same one.
quests.explanation: When we mention a noun again, we switch from 'a' to 'the'. Since the dog was already introduced, it becomes 'the dog'.

quests.question: Every evening, my family eats ___ dinner together.
quests.sentence: Every evening, my family eats ___ dinner together.
quests.hint: Meal names like breakfast, lunch, and dinner usually stand alone.
quests.explanation: Meal names such as breakfast, lunch, and dinner don't take an article in everyday sentences. We simply say 'eat dinner'.

quests.question: She adopted ___ energetic puppy from the shelter.
quests.sentence: She adopted ___ energetic puppy from the shelter.
quests.hint: Listen to the first sound in 'energetic'.
quests.explanation: 'Energetic' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'. We say 'an energetic puppy'.

quests.question: We saw a rabbit in the yard. ___ rabbit hopped under the fence.
quests.sentence: We saw a rabbit in the yard. ___ rabbit hopped under the fence.
quests.hint: This is the same rabbit named in the first sentence.
quests.explanation: Once something has been introduced with 'a', the next mention uses 'the'. 'The rabbit' points back to that exact rabbit.

quests.question: ___ cats usually sleep for most of the day.
quests.sentence: ___ cats usually sleep for most of the day.
quests.hint: This sentence talks about cats in general, not one cat.
quests.explanation: To make a general statement about a whole group, use the plain plural noun with no article. 'Cats sleep a lot' means cats in general.

quests.question: The teacher gave us ___ short quiz this morning.
quests.sentence: The teacher gave us ___ short quiz this morning.
quests.hint: 'Short' starts with a consonant sound.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before a consonant sound. 'Short' begins with 'sh', so we say 'a short quiz'.

quests.question: Open ___ window, please - it's warm in here.
quests.sentence: Open ___ window, please - it's warm in here.
quests.hint: You're both in the same room, so it's clear which one you mean.
quests.explanation: 'The' is used when the situation makes it obvious which one you mean. In a shared room, 'the window' is the one everyone can see.

quests.question: I walk to ___ school every morning with my neighbor.
quests.sentence: I walk to ___ school every morning with my neighbor.
quests.hint: Think about school as an activity, not a building here.
quests.explanation: 'Go to school' (meaning to study) is a fixed expression with no article. Compare this to 'the school', which means the actual building.

quests.question: My mother cooked ___ omelet for me this morning.
quests.sentence: My mother cooked ___ omelet for me this morning.
quests.hint: What sound does 'omelet' start with?
quests.explanation: 'Omelet' starts with a vowel sound, so it needs 'an'. We say 'an omelet', not 'a omelet'.

quests.question: I bought a loaf of bread yesterday. ___ bread is still fresh.
quests.sentence: I bought a loaf of bread yesterday. ___ bread is still fresh.
quests.hint: The bread here is the exact loaf already mentioned.
quests.explanation: Because the bread was already mentioned, the second reference uses 'the'. This shows we mean that specific loaf.

quests.question: In our house, we usually drink ___ milk with breakfast.
quests.sentence: In our house, we usually drink ___ milk with breakfast.
quests.hint: Milk can't be counted, so it doesn't need an article here.
quests.explanation: Uncountable nouns like milk, water, and juice take no article in general statements. We say 'drink milk', not 'drink a milk'.

quests.question: It's going to be ___ cold, windy day today.
quests.sentence: It's going to be ___ cold, windy day today.
quests.hint: 'Cold' starts with a consonant sound.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before a consonant sound. 'Cold' begins with 'c', so we say 'a cold, windy day'.

quests.question: Look outside - ___ sky is full of dark clouds.
quests.sentence: Look outside - ___ sky is full of dark clouds.
quests.hint: There's only one sky above us.
quests.explanation: 'The sky' is unique - there's only one, so it always takes 'the', just like 'the sun' and 'the moon'.

quests.question: In April, we usually get ___ rain almost every day.
quests.sentence: In April, we usually get ___ rain almost every day.
quests.hint: Rain is something we can't count.
quests.explanation: Uncountable nouns like rain and snow don't take an article in general statements. We say 'get rain', not 'get a rain'.

quests.question: At recess, we played ___ interesting game with a ball.
quests.sentence: At recess, we played ___ interesting game with a ball.
quests.hint: Notice the vowel sound at the start of 'interesting'.
quests.explanation: 'Interesting' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'. We say 'an interesting game'.

quests.question: That was ___ first game our team won all season.
quests.sentence: That was ___ first game our team won all season.
quests.hint: Ordinal numbers like 'first' almost always need this article.
quests.explanation: Ordinal numbers such as first, second, and last are usually paired with 'the'. We say 'the first game'.

quests.question: After school, my friends and I usually play ___ soccer in the park.
quests.sentence: After school, my friends and I usually play ___ soccer in the park.
quests.hint: Names of sports don't normally take an article.
quests.explanation: Sports and games like soccer, chess, and tennis take no article. We say 'play soccer', not 'play a soccer'.

quests.question: I just bought ___ small lamp for my desk.
quests.sentence: I just bought ___ small lamp for my desk.
quests.hint: 'Small' starts with a consonant sound.
quests.explanation: 'Small' begins with a consonant sound, so it takes 'a'. We say 'a small lamp'.

quests.question: There's a poster on my wall. ___ poster shows my favorite band.
quests.sentence: There's a poster on my wall. ___ poster shows my favorite band.
quests.hint: You already introduced this poster - point back to that same one.
quests.explanation: The second time we mention something, we usually switch to 'the'. 'The poster' refers to the exact poster named before.

quests.question: Before I go to sleep, I always go to ___ bed by ten o'clock.
quests.sentence: Before I go to sleep, I always go to ___ bed by ten o'clock.
quests.hint: 'Go to bed' is an expression about sleeping, not a piece of furniture.
quests.explanation: 'Go to bed' (meaning to sleep) is a fixed expression with no article, unlike 'the bed', which means the actual piece of furniture.

quests.question: My best friend gave me ___ amazing gift for my birthday.
quests.sentence: My best friend gave me ___ amazing gift for my birthday.
quests.hint: Listen for the vowel sound that opens 'amazing'.
quests.explanation: 'Amazing' starts with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'. We say 'an amazing gift'.

quests.question: We baked a cake for the party, and ___ cake had chocolate frosting.
quests.sentence: We baked a cake for the party, and ___ cake had chocolate frosting.
quests.hint: This cake is the very one mentioned earlier in the sentence.
quests.explanation: Because the cake was already introduced, we now call it 'the cake'. This shows it's the same one, not a new one.

quests.question: At birthday parties, guests usually sing ___ songs and eat cake.
quests.sentence: At birthday parties, guests usually sing ___ songs and eat cake.
quests.hint: This is about songs in general, not one specific song.
quests.explanation: General statements about plural nouns use no article. 'Sing songs' refers to the activity in general.

quests.question: The shop assistant showed me ___ warm winter scarf.
quests.sentence: The shop assistant showed me ___ warm winter scarf.
quests.hint: 'Warm' starts with a consonant sound.
quests.explanation: Words starting with a consonant sound take 'a'. 'Warm' begins with 'w', so we say 'a warm scarf'.

quests.question: I tried on three jackets, and this red one was ___ nicest.
quests.sentence: I tried on three jackets, and this red one was ___ nicest.
quests.hint: Comparing this jacket to all the others calls for a superlative.
quests.explanation: Superlatives like 'the nicest' or 'the best' always take 'the'. We're comparing this jacket to every other one we tried.

quests.question: On weekends, my mother likes to go ___ shopping downtown.
quests.sentence: On weekends, my mother likes to go ___ shopping downtown.
quests.hint: 'Go shopping' is a fixed expression.
quests.explanation: Activities like 'go shopping', 'go swimming', and 'go fishing' are set phrases with no article before the -ing word.

quests.question: The doctor said I have ___ ear infection.
quests.sentence: The doctor said I have ___ ear infection.
quests.hint: What sound does 'ear' start with?
quests.explanation: 'Ear' starts with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'. We say 'an ear infection'.

quests.question: I have a small cut on my hand. ___ cut isn't too deep.
quests.sentence: I have a small cut on my hand. ___ cut isn't too deep.
quests.hint: You're referring back to the exact cut just described.
quests.explanation: The second mention of something already introduced takes 'the'. 'The cut' points to that specific cut.

quests.question: To stay healthy, you should drink plenty of ___ water every day.
quests.sentence: To stay healthy, you should drink plenty of ___ water every day.
quests.hint: Water can't be counted, so no article is needed.
quests.explanation: Uncountable nouns like water take no article in general advice. We say 'drink water', not 'drink a water'.
